task.title: Mkdir loses os.ModeSticky on Linux
task.body:
On Linux, `localDirectory.Mkdir(name, 0o700 | os.ModeSticky)` succeeds but creates a directory without the sticky bit. `Directory.Mkdir` is documented as equivalent to `os.Mkdir`, which preserves that bit.

The Unix adapter casts `os.FileMode` directly to `uint32`. Go's `os.ModeSticky` and the kernel's `S_ISVTX` use different bit positions, so passing the former to `mkdirat()` loses it.

Reproduced against main at ff9af3883025f517a42725cb66b1a11cc33ea4c2 on Linux x86_64: create a local directory handle, call `Mkdir` with `0o700 | os.ModeSticky`, then inspect the new directory with `os.Stat`. Expected mode: `os.ModeDir | 0o700 | os.ModeSticky`. Actual mode omits `os.ModeSticky`.

I have a small mode-conversion fix and tests covering the resulting mode, umasks including 0700/0777, and refusal to modify existing directories or symlinks. The mode and umask cases fail on the original code and pass with the fix. This report concerns Linux; BSD systems strip sticky bits during directory creation and need a separate approach.
